content.value_statement: Teams need consistent .NET backend patterns for APIs, data access, security, and background work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical ASP.NET Core service implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of ASP.NET Core 8+ Minimal API and controller-based endpoints.
Applies Entity Framework Core patterns for DbContext setup, queries, migrations, and DTO projection.
Provides authentication and authorization guidance for JWT, Identity, OAuth 2.0, and policy-based access.
Supports background worker design with IHostedService, BackgroundService, Hangfire, and Quartz.NET.
Recommends production API practices such as validation, exception handling, health checks, Swagger, and structured logging.
limitations: It focuses on backend service code and does not cover frontend application implementation.
It assumes modern ASP.NET Core 8+ patterns and may need adjustment for older .NET Framework projects.
It does not provide cloud-provider deployment details unless the user asks for them.
It gives implementation guidance but does not replace project-specific security review or load testing.

use_cases.title: Create a New API Service
use_cases.description: Generate a clean ASP.NET Core API structure with endpoints, validation, persistence, and OpenAPI support.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Data Access
use_cases.description: Refactor EF Core queries, DTO projections, tracking behavior, and DbContext usage for safer performance.

use_cases.title: Add Secure Service Features
use_cases.description: Design JWT authentication, authorization policies, background workers, health checks, and structured logging.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new API route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dotnet-backend skill to add an ASP.NET Core endpoint for [resource]. Include request validation, response DTOs, and EF Core persistence.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Data Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for an existing service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dotnet-backend skill to review this EF Core query flow. Improve tracking behavior, projection, async usage, and transaction boundaries where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Add Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for secure access control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dotnet-backend skill to design JWT authentication and policy-based authorization for these roles, claims, endpoints, and token requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dotnet-backend skill to harden this ASP.NET Core service with validation, exception handling, health checks, structured logging, background jobs, and tests.

output_examples.input: Add a users API with EF Core persistence and password hashing.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with endpoint shape, DTO names, validation rules, DbContext changes, and security notes for password handling.

output_examples.input: Review this controller and improve performance.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering async queries, AsNoTracking usage, DTO projection, logging scope, validation gaps, and focused test recommendations.

output_examples.input: Add a background email sender to an existing service.
output_examples.output: A service design describing scoped dependency usage, cancellation handling, retry behavior, logging, persistence updates, and operational safeguards.

best_practices: Provide current project structure, target .NET version, database provider, and authentication requirements before asking for implementation.
Ask for tests and migration impact when the change touches persistence, authentication, or background processing.
Review generated security-sensitive code for project policies, secret handling, authorization rules, and compliance requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad backend rewrites without naming the affected endpoints, entities, and acceptance criteria.
Do not accept authentication or authorization code without checking token settings, claim rules, and failure behavior.
Do not mix frontend UI requests with this skill unless they directly support backend contract design.

faq.question: What kind of .NET projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports ASP.NET Core 8+ backend APIs, Minimal APIs, controller-based Web APIs, EF Core services, and background workers.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers JWT, ASP.NET Core Identity, OAuth 2.0, Azure AD, roles, claims, and policy-based authorization.

faq.question: Does it generate database migrations?
faq.answer: It can guide EF Core migration design and commands, but migrations should be reviewed and run in the project environment.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review async usage, query tracking, DTO projection, caching, connection use, and API response patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover deployment?
faq.answer: It covers production readiness patterns, but cloud-specific deployment is outside scope unless the user provides that requirement.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill safely?
faq.answer: Yes. The reviewed content is instructional and does not contain malicious commands or prompt injection attempts.
